set_title: Pericarditis vs endocarditis names: which layer and what is growing on the valve
stem: A 22-year-old man has sharp chest pain that eases when he sits forward and worsens when he lies flat. ECG shows diffuse ST elevation in most leads.
oneliner: 22-year-old man, chest pain better sitting forward, diffuse ST elevation → ?

whyNot.B: Chronic scarring with Kussmaul sign; this is **acute pain with diffuse ST elevation**
whyNot.C: Needs fever and a new murmur; he has **pain easing when sitting forward**
whyNot.D: Sterile lupus valve growths; he has **positional chest pain and diffuse ST elevation**
whyNot.E: Follows strep with migratory arthritis; he has **pain easing when sitting forward**

why: Peri- (around) + cardium (heart) + -itis (inflammation): inflamed sac around the heart. **Pain eased by sitting forward with diffuse ST elevation** is classic.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **Pain better leaning forward; diffuse ST elevation**
**Advanced cancer; sterile clots on closure line**
post-strep inflammation of all heart layers

idea.rule: Peri = around the heart; endo = inside, on the valves.
also: Diffuse ST elevation with PR depression

set_title: Pericarditis vs endocarditis names: which layer and what is growing on the valve
stem: A 30-year-old man who injects drugs has 5 days of fever and chills. He has a new holosystolic murmur at the left lower sternal border, and chest x-ray shows several peripheral nodular opacities.
oneliner: 30-year-old man, injection drug use, fever, new tricuspid murmur → ?

whyNot.A: Causes positional pain and a rub; he has a **new tricuspid murmur and fever**
whyNot.B: Sterile lupus growths; he has **fever, injection drug use and lung nodules**
whyNot.C: Sterile cancer-related growths; he has **fever and injection drug use**
whyNot.E: Follows strep pharyngitis with arthritis; he has **injection drug use and lung nodules**

why: Endo- (inside) + cardium (heart) + -itis, with infective meaning microbes: infected heart lining. **Injection drug use, fever and a new tricuspid murmur** point to it.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **Pain better leaning forward; diffuse ST elevation**
**Advanced cancer; sterile clots on closure line**
post-strep inflammation of all heart layers

idea.rule: Infective endocarditis = microbes on a valve; lupus and cancer forms are sterile.
also: Injection drug use: tricuspid valve, S. aureus

set_title: Thrombo- names: clots vs too few or too many platelets
stem: A 35-year-old man who smokes 2 packs daily has pain in both feet at rest and ulcers on three fingertips. Brachial and femoral pulses are normal, and he has had two episodes of tender cord-like superficial veins. Platelet count is normal.
oneliner: 35-year-old heavy smoker, fingertip ulcers, foot rest pain, tender superficial veins → ?

whyNot.A: Causes fever, confusion and hemolysis; his **platelet count is normal**
whyNot.B: Presents with bleeding and low platelets; his **platelet count is normal**
whyNot.C: Needs heparin exposure and falling platelets; his **platelet count is normal**
whyNot.D: Platelets exceed 450,000/mm3; his **platelet count is normal**

why: Thrombo- (clot) + angi- (vessel) + -itis, obliterans (closing off): clotting vessel inflammation. **A young heavy smoker with fingertip ulcers and superficial vein clots** fits.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **Recurrent clots in different veins; pancreatic cancer**

idea.rule: Buerger = young male smoker, distal ischemia, migratory superficial vein clots.
also: Segmental small-vessel inflammation; quitting smoking is key

set_title: Ka- names: Kawasaki, Kaposi, Kasabach-Merritt, Kartagener, Kallmann
stem: A 3-year-old boy has had fever for 6 days, bilateral nonexudative conjunctivitis, cracked red lips with a strawberry tongue, cervical lymphadenopathy, a polymorphous rash and swollen hands. Platelets are 620,000/mm3.
oneliner: 3-year-old boy, fever 6 days, red eyes, strawberry tongue, swollen hands → ?

whyNot.A: A purple vascular tumor in AIDS; he has **fever, red eyes and strawberry tongue**
whyNot.B: Causes low platelets in a vascular tumor; his platelets are **high at 620,000/mm3**
whyNot.C: Causes sinusitis and dextrocardia; he has **fever, conjunctivitis and swollen hands**
whyNot.E: Causes absent puberty and anosmia; he has **fever with strawberry tongue**

why: Named for Tomisaku Kawasaki: medium-vessel vasculitis in children. **Fever for 5+ days with conjunctivitis, strawberry tongue, adenopathy, rash and swollen hands** fit.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: eponym: platelets trapped in vascular tumor
eponym: ciliary dyskinesia with situs inversus
eponym: GnRH neurons fail to migrate

idea.rule: Kawasaki = fever 5+ days plus CRASH features; treat with IVIG and aspirin.
also: Coronary artery aneurysm is the complication
CRASH: conjunctivitis, rash, adenopathy, strawberry tongue, hand swelling

set_title: -ectasia words: something widened (telangiectasia, duct ectasia, lymphangiectasia)
stem: A 40-year-old man has had repeated nosebleeds since adolescence. He has small red spots on his lips and tongue. His father has the same nosebleeds.
oneliner: 40-year-old man, nosebleeds since adolescence + red lip spots + father the same → ?

whyNot.A: Ataxia-telangiectasia is recessive and starts with gait ataxia; his **father has the same nosebleeds**
whyNot.B: Mammary duct ectasia is a breast disease; he has **nosebleeds and lip spots**
whyNot.D: Intestinal lymphangiectasia causes diarrhea and edema; he has **nosebleeds with lip spots**
whyNot.E: Telangiectasia macularis eruptiva perstans is cutaneous mastocytosis; he has **nosebleeds with lip spots**

why: Hemorrhagic + telangiectasia (widened tiny vessels): inherited, autosomal dominant. **Recurrent nosebleeds, lip spots and an affected father** point to hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia.

idea.rule: Telangiectasia = widened tiny vessels; the first word names the setting.
also: Lung AVMs can cause brain abscess

set_title: Acro- names: things at the ends of the body (hands, feet, face)
stem: A 1-day-old term girl has blue hands and feet. Her lips and trunk are pink, she feeds well, and oxygen saturation is 98%. The blue color fades when her hands are warmed.
oneliner: 1-day-old term girl, blue hands and feet + pink lips and trunk + SpO2 98% + fades with warming → ?

whyNot.A: Acromegaly is adult hormone excess; she is a **newborn with warm-reversible color change**
whyNot.B: Acrodermatitis enteropathica has scaly rash and diarrhea; she has **only blue hands and feet**
whyNot.C: Acrochordon is a skin tag; hers are **bluish hands and feet fading with warming**
whyNot.D: Acral lentiginous melanoma is an adult lesion; hers is a **transient newborn color change**

why: Acro (extremity) + cyanosis (blue): peripheral vasoconstriction in the first days of life. **Blue hands and feet with pink trunk and normal saturation** is benign.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **High IGF-1; GH not suppressed by glucose**

idea.rule: Acrocyanosis: peripheral blue with pink lips; central cyanosis is the dangerous one.
also: Blue lips or trunk means central cyanosis

set_title: Fetal remnant ligament names: arteriosum vs venosum vs teres vs medial vs median
stem: A 45-year-old man has sudden left-sided weakness. Three days earlier he had a long flight and now has a swollen painful right calf, confirmed as deep vein thrombosis. Echocardiography with agitated saline shows bubbles crossing into the left atrium at the interatrial septum.
oneliner: 45M, DVT then stroke + bubbles cross atrial septum → septal remnant that failed to seal → ?
ask: Which structure marks the remnant of the opening involved here?

whyNot.B: Median umbilical ligament is a urachus remnant; his shunt is **between the atria**
whyNot.C: Ligamentum arteriosum connects aorta and pulmonary artery; his shunt is **at the atrial septum**
whyNot.D: Medial umbilical ligaments are arterial remnants; his bubbles cross **an atrial flap**
whyNot.E: Ligamentum teres hepatis lies in the falciform ligament; his bubbles cross **the atrial septum**

why: Fossa ovalis is the depression where the foramen ovale closed. **A flap that stays open lets a vein clot cross to the brain** (paradoxical embolism).

idea.rule: Fossa ovalis = closed foramen ovale; PFO = it fails.
also: Right atrial pressure rise opens a PFO

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **In falciform ligament; paraumbilical veins: caput medusae**

set_title: Fetal remnant ligament names: arteriosum vs venosum vs teres vs medial vs median
stem: A 12-year-old boy undergoes repair of aortic coarctation. The surgeon divides a fibrous cord running from the proximal left pulmonary artery to the underside of the aortic arch. After surgery his voice is hoarse, and laryngoscopy shows left vocal cord paralysis.
oneliner: 12M, coarctation repair + cord from left pulmonary artery to aortic arch divided, then hoarse voice → ?
ask: Which ligament did the surgeon divide?

whyNot.A: Medial umbilical ligaments lie in the abdomen; this joins **aorta and pulmonary artery**
whyNot.B: Ligamentum teres hepatis is in the liver edge; this one is **in the chest**
whyNot.D: Fossa ovalis is an atrial depression; this is **a ligament between great vessels**
whyNot.E: Ligamentum venosum is in the liver fissure; this one **joins great vessels**

why: Arteriosum = artery. The ductus arteriosus closes into this ligament. **The left recurrent laryngeal nerve loops beneath it**, so injury causes hoarseness.

idea.rule: Ligamentum arteriosum = ductus arteriosus; left recurrent laryngeal nerve loops under it.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **In falciform ligament; paraumbilical veins: caput medusae**
